_comment: Carino Hardware build profiles. Edit freely. A spec's `eg` is a list of example models; each item is either a plain string or {"t":"name","link":"https://…"} to link a specific model. Mark the single most important spec with "key": true. Bump `updated` (YYYY-MM) whenever you refresh the example parts/prices — it's shown on the page so readers know how fresh the models are.

profiles.name: Budget / Everyday
profiles.tagline: Web, docs, video and light multitasking. Integrated graphics are plenty.
profiles.key: An SSD and dual-channel RAM change how the machine feels far more than the CPU — and both are cheap.

specs.note: Dual-channel — two matched sticks, not one (8 GB is the floor).
Intel UHD / AMD Radeon — no add-in card needed.
Never a mechanical boot drive in the 2020s.
Efficiency tier matters more than raw watts here.

profiles.name: Business / Office
profiles.tagline: Fleet-friendly productivity, video calls, dozens of tabs, remotely manageable.
profiles.key: For fleets, manageability (vPro/DASH) and TPM 2.0 matter more than raw speed.

specs.note: 32 GB if you live in a browser + IDE + a VM or two.
Discrete only for CAD / light 3D.
Pair with automated backup, not RAID.
TPM required for Win 11 / BitLocker; vPro adds remote out-of-band control.

profiles.name: Gaming
profiles.tagline: High frame-rates at 1080p / 1440p. The GPU is the star — buy VRAM.
profiles.key: The GPU and its VRAM set your resolution and detail ceiling — spend there first, then the CPU.

specs.note: CL30 kit; 3D V-Cache chips love fast memory.
DirectStorage-ready for fast level loads.
Headroom for GPU transient spikes.
Holds boost clocks under sustained load.

profiles.name: Content Creation
profiles.tagline: 4K editing, rendering, photo & 3D. Cores, VRAM and fast scratch storage.
profiles.key: Cores shorten renders, VRAM enables effects and resolution, and a calibrated display keeps color honest.

specs.note: Timelines, layers and 3D scenes eat memory fast.
Hardware encode/decode slashes export times.
Fast scratch/cache drive + cheap archive.
Calibrated IPS/OLED; DCI-P3 for HDR grading.
Stable through long renders.

profiles.name: Enthusiast / Halo
profiles.key: No bottlenecks: flagship GPU, top CPU, fast tuned memory, and cooling that never throttles.

specs.note: EXPO / XMP tuned.
~12 GB/s sequential.
Native 12VHPWR connector.
Quiet at full tilt.

profiles.name: Home Lab / Server
profiles.tagline: VMs, containers, NAS, 24/7 uptime. Prioritise ECC, PCIe lanes and I/O.
profiles.key: ECC memory and out-of-band management (IPMI) matter more than peak speed for anything that runs unattended.

specs.note: Error-correcting — essential for ZFS and long uptime.
Out-of-band mgmt + drive bays + PCIe lanes.
Redundant ZFS vdevs; HBA in IT mode.
Intel NIC preferred for driver stability.
Sized for spin-up surge.

profiles.name: Local AI / LLM
profiles.tagline: Running models locally. VRAM (or unified memory) is everything — it caps model size.
profiles.key: VRAM — or Apple unified memory — is the whole game: it sets the largest model you can run. Everything else is secondary.

specs.note: VRAM caps the model size you can load; overflow to system RAM is drastically slower.
Shared RAM runs large models without a discrete GPU.
For CPU offload and dataset staging.
Feeds the GPU; rarely the inference bottleneck.
Model weights are huge — a 70B model ≈ 40–140 GB.
≈ 450 W per high-end GPU + headroom.

glossary: Cores vs clock
Cores = parallel jobs (rendering, VMs, compiling). Clock/IPC = speed of one job (most games, single-thread apps). Games want fewer fast cores; creation wants many.
VRAM
GPU memory. It caps what fits: texture detail, resolution, and — critically — the size of an AI model you can run. When it overflows, performance falls off a cliff.
DDR4 vs DDR5
DDR5 has more bandwidth and higher clocks; DDR4 is cheaper and mature. Always run dual-channel (matched pair) — a single stick halves memory bandwidth.
ECC memory
Error-correcting RAM catches bit-flips in flight. Overkill for gaming, essential for servers, ZFS storage, and anything running unattended for months.
NVMe Gen3/4/5
PCIe SSD generations: Gen3 ≈ 3.5 GB/s, Gen4 ≈ 7 GB/s, Gen5 ≈ 12 GB/s. Real-world app launches barely differ; big sequential copies and DirectStorage benefit.
TLC vs QLC / DRAM cache
TLC endures more writes than QLC; a DRAM cache keeps speed up under sustained load. For a boot/scratch drive, prefer TLC-with-DRAM over cheap DRAM-less QLC.
PSU 80+ rating
Efficiency tier (Bronze→Titanium) — less wasted heat. Size for peak GPU transients (can briefly 2× rated draw); ATX 3.0 handles 12VHPWR spikes natively.
TDP / cooling
Thermal Design Power ≈ heat to dissipate. Under-cooled chips throttle and lose the performance you paid for. Match cooler to sustained, not rated, load.
iGPU vs dGPU
Integrated graphics share system RAM — fine for desktop, media, light gaming. A discrete card has its own VRAM and is required for serious gaming, 3D, and AI.
TPM 2.0 / vPro
TPM 2.0 is a security chip (required by Windows 11, BitLocker). vPro/DASH add remote out-of-band management — matters for fleets, not home users.
